subject: Hosted inference: US-West latency spike — status page message and mitigation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference: US-West latency spike — status page message and mitigation

Team,

We observed a regional p95/p99 latency spike impacting hosted text-generation requests in US-West starting ~08:50 PDT. The on-call bridge is up; engineering has identified routing pressure against a bulkhead pool that caused failover to a degraded capacity tier. Impact: ~6% of customer requests experienced elevated token latency (~2-6s extra per token) between 08:50 and 10:30 PDT, with transient additional retries through 11:05 PDT.

I’ve drafted an initial status page blurb (attached: statuspage-draft-20260831.md). Please review quickly — we need to publish a clear note within the hour to affected customers and to minimize duplicate support tickets. Key items to confirm:
- root cause statement: bulkhead isolation + misapplied gateway rate-limiter config
- impact window and % of requests/users affected
- mitigation status and ETA for full normalization

Short asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm the root cause language and whether we can say "no customer data loss"?
- Ben: please review the mitigation steps and ETA bullets in the draft (I attached a CSV timeline).
- Laura: want you on the outbound to Greenvale Labs and a couple of other tier-1 accounts — I’ll loop you in after we publish.

Attachments: statuspage-draft-20260831.md, mitigation-timeline.csv

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference: US-West latency spike — status page message and mitigation

Jonas,

Quick update from the bridge: engineering confirmed the immediate cause is a misapplied rate-limit rule in the API gateway that reduced available headroom for the primary bulkhead pool. Traffic was spilled to a smaller, older capacity pool with higher CPU contention and different quantization profiles, which produced the elevated per-token latency.

Important notes for the status page:
- Please avoid deep infra jargon. Say: "A routing configuration caused a subset of requests to be served from a degraded capacity pool, leading to increased response times for some customers."
- Confirmed: no user payloads were dropped or lost; all requests were processed (some with retries).
- Root cause timeline: rule deployed at 08:42 PDT, symptom start at ~08:50, mitigation (roll-back and routing correction) started at 09:12, full normalization at 11:05.

We attached a short ops log excerpt (ops-bridge-log-snippet.txt) that shows the gateway rule change and the pool failover events. Suggest the status page contain: impact + what we did + next steps (postmortem + follow-up with affected customers).

Ben, ETA on a concise mitigation bulleted timeline? If we can publish with a small table of events that will reduce follow-ups.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Support Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Sara Khan <sara@greenvalelabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference: US-West latency spike — status page message and mitigation

Jonas / Laura,

Thanks for the heads up and for the quick work. We saw a spike in response times around 09:00 PDT for our inference calls and had some timeouts at our client side. Two quick questions:

1) Did any of the retries result in duplicate outputs being stored on our end? We write outputs to our user event log, and we want to understand whether we should dedupe.
2) Will we get a postmortem with timing and mitigation details we can share with our reliability team?

We're not seeing lost requests in our logs but saw several client retry attempts from a small percentage of our hosts. Appreciate the follow-up.

Best,
Sara Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Greenvale Labs
sara@greenvalelabs.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Khan <sara@greenvalelabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference: US-West latency spike — status page message and mitigation

Sara — thanks for the questions and for flagging what you observed. Quick answers below; formal postmortem coming by EOD tomorrow and we'll share a doc link.

1) Duplicate outputs: our logs show no message duplication on the service side. Short explanation: retries were client-side and resulted in multiple inbound attempts, but our request de-duplication token prevented duplicate processing for the vast majority of replayed requests. We will provide an event-level summary in the postmortem for any borderline cases, but you should not expect many duplicates. If you prefer, we can share a short list of sample request ids from your tenant for you to verify against your event log.

2) Postmortem: we are drafting a full incident report with timeline, root cause, and remediation actions (permanent config guardrails, improved pre-deploy checks, and a runway for more gradual gateway rule rollout). Draft link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xpostmortem-draft. Final will be published after internal review but we plan to share a sanitized copy with affected customers tomorrow.

Actions for Greenvale Labs:
- If you want sample request ids for cross-checking, please reply and we'll generate a short export.
- We'll schedule a brief 30-min sync with your reliability team this week if helpful — Laura, can you coordinate availability?

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the rapid context. We'll follow up with the final report and any additional artifacts (gateway diffs, log slices).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
